ALLEGATION_VERDICT: NOT_REAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/cex-limit-point-compact-without-countable-compactness.md, steps 2.1 and 3.1
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: “So $p$ is a limit point of $A$, and in particular every infinite subset of $X$ has one: $X$ is limit point compact.” “This is the hypothesis of claim 4 of [[thm-compactness-variants-hierarchy]], and steps 2.1 and 2.2 show that dropping it makes the implication fail.”
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: “Why claim 4 needs the singleton hypothesis and claim 1(c) does not. A limit point of the set $A$ built at step 2.1 need not be one of the $x_n$ with large index unless the finitely many early terms can be cut away, and cutting them away is exactly what closedness of singletons permits. Without that hypothesis the implication fails, and the witness is worked on this page's companion, as `cex-limit-point-compact-without-countable-compactness`: a space in which every nonempty subset has a limit point, for the trivial reason that each point has a partner it cannot be separated from, and which has a countable open cover with no finite subcover.”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The rejection names no actual defect. It mistakes a stronger conclusion for a gap: step 2.1 proves the required limit point condition because every infinite subset is nonempty. Step 3.1 correctly establishes failure of the singleton-closed hypothesis, and the cited theorem explicitly identifies this exact companion witness. No claim or citation is unlicensed.

OTHER_FINDINGS: NONE
